title: Categorical degree-zero Cech cocycles give compatible local morphisms
statement: For an abelian-group-valued presheaf P on C, a family of arrows pi_i : U_i -> X, and an abelian group E, any morphism z from E to the categorical product of singleton-product presheaf values killed by the first Mathlib Cech differential gives compatible morphisms to P(U_i). For a : W -> U_i and b : W -> U_j with a pi_i = b pi_j, extract the i and j components of z and identify singleton products with U_i and U_j using their diagonal inverses; the resulting morphisms agree after restriction along a and b. No covering or sheaf hypothesis is needed.

source.place: Tags 03AM and 03AN; first Cech differential and zero-cocycle compatibility

proof.text: Expand the first alternating coface differential as delta_0 minus delta_1. Project z d^0 = 0 to the tuple (i,j), using the FormalCoproduct evaluation product-projection equation. The two resulting restrictions to the pair product agree.
The two maps from Fin 1 to Fin 2 skipping 0 and 1 are respectively constant 1 and constant 0. Thus the coface maps are the product lifts of the pair projections to singleton products.

Construct the arrow from W over X to the pair product by the finite product universal property, using a pi_i = b pi_j. Its composites with the singleton coface maps are a followed by the singleton diagonal and b followed by the singleton diagonal. Restrict the projected equation along this arrow and use presheaf functoriality.

lean.statement:
theorem cech_zero_cocycle_compatibility
    {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] [HasFiniteWidePullbacks C]
    (P : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ AddCommGrpCat.{v}) (X : C)
    {ι : Type v} {U : ι → C} (π : ∀ i, U i ⟶ X)
    {E : AddCommGrpCat.{v}}
    (z : E ⟶ ∏ᶜ (fun s : Fin 1 → ι ↦
      P.obj (op (∏ᶜ (fun k ↦ Over.mk (π (s k)))).left)))
    (hz : z ≫ ((cechComplexFunctor (fun i ↦ Over.mk (π i))).obj
      ((Over.forget X).op ⋙ P)).d 0 1 = 0)
    {W : C} {i j : ι} (a : W ⟶ U i) (b : W ⟶ U j)
    (hab : a ≫ π i = b ≫ π j) :
    z ≫ Pi.π (fun s : Fin 1 → ι ↦
      P.obj (op (∏ᶜ (fun k ↦ Over.mk (π (s k)))).left)) (fun _ ↦ i) ≫
        P.map (Pi.lift (fun _ : Fin 1 ↦ 𝟙 (Over.mk (π i)))).left.op ≫ P.map a.op =
    z ≫ Pi.π (fun s : Fin 1 → ι ↦
      P.obj (op (∏ᶜ (fun k ↦ Over.mk (π (s k)))).left)) (fun _ ↦ j) ≫
        P.map (Pi.lift (fun _ : Fin 1 ↦ 𝟙 (Over.mk (π j)))).left.op ≫ P.map b.op
